answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post offers, with rewards and penalties tied to the same on-chain record. If several identities coordinate, their deposits remain visible through a kernel of linked transactions; a default or proven fraud can trigger slashing across those accounts, sending a ripple through their shared collateral. A mirror account does not create free influence: every extra identity needs another lock, so a sybil attacker must immobilize real capital and risks losing it.
